title: Choose the visual world for Anchor Studio by DNL
question: The roll assigned Contact Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show the Visuals page (VO 1 of the Moscow story).

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: the photo editor's contact sheet: black film rebate, edge-print numbers, red china-marker selects
options.thesis: Every story is a roll; picking pictures is marking the sheet, timing is the edge print.
options.viewport: Section rail left, contact-sheet grid of frames centre with frame codes in amber mono, picked frames looped in red with their play-order number, picked list and fill bar right.
options.risk: The hand-drawn loop must stay a crisp state mark; overdone it reads as a craft costume on a working tool.

raised.raise: Section rail heights are proportional to each section's seconds, so the script's shape is visible at a glance.
Every frame keeps one stable code (R03·F12) used on the sheet, the picked list, the timeline and the clip viewer.
All neutrals come from one eleven-step graphite ramp; no stray greys.
In the clip viewer the next moment is preloaded, one key away.
Every locked Continue says exactly what is ahead and how much is missing, in seconds.

options.label: On-Air Package
options.lineage: the broadcast graphics package: red kicker chips, white straps, ticker crawl
options.thesis: The studio speaks in the channel's own on-air grammar: straps for headings, a ticker for status.
options.viewport: Navy shell, section headings as lower-third straps with red kicker chips, a red ticker crawl along the bottom carrying voice, fill and queue status.
options.risk: Most familiar to the desk, and the chrome competes with the real lower thirds on the preview; status in a crawl is slower to read.

options.label: Dark Console
options.thesis: Persistent graphite panels split by hairline seams; colour only for state.
options.viewport: Three persistent panels: sections with status, found footage, picked list; navigation changes panel contents.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity; loses audience identification: nothing in it is a newsroom's.
options.risk: Reads as a developer tool; nothing says news or DNL.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each decision point shows only the choices ahead.
options.viewport: Yellow bands per step with what is ahead.
options.case: Loses both axes: yellow ground breaks the pinned dark tool; editors don't read their work as a terminal.
options.kept: Every gate states what is ahead and how far.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.case: Loses both axes: paper-manual layering fights a dense video tool.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels hide meaning editors need at a glance.
options.kept: A stable number for every artifact.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.case: Loses both axes: hatching and sliding sheets slow a desk tool.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: Loses both axes: editors compare many shots at once.
options.kept: The next item is preloaded, one step away.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark non-linear editor: media pool, viewer, inspector, timeline.
canonCard.viewport: Media pool, viewer, inspector, timeline below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any video editor by design.
